h: Megillas Rus on the Second Day: Yom Tov Sheni and Torah She'b'al Peh

p: Now, it is the custom to read Megillas Rus
on the second day of Shavuos.
And the Magen Avraham (beginning of siman 494)
cites in the name of the Yefeh Mareh
a resolution of what he asked:
the Torah was given, after all,
on the fifty-first day of the Sefirah,
yet on the fiftieth day of the Sefirah we say
עַל יוֹם טוֹב שֵׁנִי שֶׁל גָּלֻיּוֹת.
to Yom Tov Sheni shel Galuyos.
Now this needs to be understood:
after all, the main Yom Tov
is the first day of Yom Tov,
אֵין עוֹשִׂין כְּלָל יוֹם טוֹב שֵׁנִי
they do not keep a second day of Yom Tov at all
מַה שֶּׁנִּרְמָז יוֹם טוֹב שֵׁנִי שֶׁל גָּלֻיּוֹת
that Yom Tov Sheni shel Galuyos is alluded to
is based on what we have said,
that on Shavuos, Zman Matan Toraseinu,
the time when the Torah was given —
from the side of the Tree of Life.
the aspect of Torah she'b'al peh,
which is forty-nine ways of ruling pure
and forty-nine ways of ruling impure.
so that thereby they will merit

And this is the matter of Yom Tov Sheni as well,
which is by the command of the Sages
and the power of Torah she'b'al peh:
in the fixing of the month,
by the command of the Sages

וְזֶה הוּא יוֹם טוֹב שֵׁנִי שֶׁל גָּלֻיּוֹת:

paragraphs.text: Magen Avraham, Orach Chaim 494 (opening) — "And the further difficulty — that the Torah was given on the fifty-first day of the Omer, since they left Egypt on Thursday and the Torah was given on Shabbos — the Yefeh Mar'eh already answered: it comes to allude to us the second Yom Tov of the Diaspora; and perhaps this is what is meant by 'Moshe added one day on his own.'"

paragraphs.text: Parallel: Pri Tzaddik, Motza'ei Yom Kippur 6 — “So too on Shavuos, the time of Matan Torah: only on that day is there the resting of the giving of the Written Torah; and even though they said (Sifrei, Eikev), ‘Every day let them be new in your eyes,’ that is another matter, for this is the power of the renewal of the Oral Torah, which is renewed every day in the souls of Israel, each according to his aspect.” Connection: Both passages treat the theme “every year on Shavuos the merit is awakened to attain words of Torah from the side of the Tree of Life”; both separate the day of the Written Torah from the Oral Torah's daily renewal.

p: "And on Shavuos, which is Matan Torah,
when the two Tablets of the Torah were given
from the side of the Tree of Life,
one must offer corresponding to them
which are the two letters hei, hei."
מְרַמֵּז עַל אוֹתִיּוֹת י׳ ו׳ מֵהַשֵּׁם.

and "You shall have no other gods,"
by which the yetzer hara was uprooted from their hearts
(כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ שִׁיר הַשִּׁירִים רַבָּה א, ב);
and "You shall not take the Name in vain,"
which stands against the power of the yetzer hara,
which is able to hide itself
and to disguise itself as one who guides toward good,
the Name of Hashem and the honor of Heaven
will be further exalted and uplifted.

paragraphs.text: Zohar III 61a (Acharei Mos) — "What is Kodesh? The completeness of all, called supernal Chochmah; from this place the holy anointing oil flows along known paths to the place called supernal Binah, and from there springs and streams go forth on every side… And when this Zos is blessed from that supernal place called Kodesh… they call her Ruach HaKodesh — a spirit from that Kodesh." A parallel appears in Haazinu (Zohar III 297a).
